note: A MANUAL DONATION WROTE A CRM NOTE AND NOTHING ELSE. The founder: "If I add a donation from a user in CRM it updates the CRM but not the dashboard." There were TWO records of a gift and only ONE of them counted. `tenants/{t}/invoices` is THE money ledger - the Overview tab sums it through `toInvoiceRow`/`readableReceipts`, AdminAccounting reads it, `/api/giving-statements/generate` aggregates it per donor per year, and `/api/donation-history` is how a MEMBER retrieves their own receipts - and until this ticket its only writer was `lib/donation-webhook.ts`. AdminCRM's Add Activity -> Donation wrote a `contactActivities` row and bumped `contacts.totalDonated`, and nothing downstream reads either as money, so THE-249's own disclaimer ("open their contact, press Add Activity, choose Donation") led nowhere but that contact's timeline. `lib/manual-donation.ts` now writes the SAME `donation_receipt` invoice the webhook writes - `type`, cents, an ISO `issuedAt` and `recipientEmail` as the identity key - so one manual entry reaches the dashboard figure, accounting, the giving statement, the member's own history and their per-year totals with NO new reader anywhere. THE WRITER IS SERVER-SIDE AND firestore.rules IS UNTOUCHED, which is the answer to this ticket's STOP condition 2 rather than a dodge: the invoices rule is `hasPermission('manageAccounting', tenantId)` and the admin who records a gift holds `manageCRM`, so a CLIENT write would be refused for exactly the people doing the recording, and loosening the rule would hand every CRM admin direct write access to the money ledger in a file that AUTO-DEPLOYS on merge with no emulator tests (THE-313's one line turned 46 files red). The write therefore goes through the Admin SDK behind `/api/donations/manual`, which imposes `requireTenantPermission(request, tenantId, 'manageCRM')` itself - the documented use for that helper, "admin-moderation API routes that stand in for a client write the rules can't express" - and the rule is ASSERTED as it stands so the suite goes red the day it moves. THE-350 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere. NO COMPOSITE INDEX IS REQUIRED (STOP condition 5): the writer performs one `get()` by document id and one `add()` and builds no query at all, so `firestore.indexes.json` - which does not deploy, and where an index would be inert while the query threw `failed-precondition` in production - is untouched and asserted byte-identical alongside `functions/` and `src/app/layout.tsx`. THE issuedAt DISAGREEMENT IS REAL, PRE-EXISTING AND REPORTED, NOT CREATED HERE (STOP condition 3): `dashboard-data.ts`, `giving-data.ts`, `form-answers.ts`, `bounded-list-read.ts`, `service-plan.ts`, `rota-invitations.ts`, `month-view.ts` and `useVolunteerRotaQueries.ts` all already record that `invoices.issuedAt` holds BOTH ISO strings and Timestamps and that Firestore orders across types by TYPE FIRST. Every LIVE writer of the field in `src/` writes an ISO string - the three `issuedAt: nowIso` sites in `donation-webhook.ts` are the only ones, and this ticket's is the fourth - so the Timestamp rows are historical data with no producer left. Normalising them is a migration and the founder's call; this ticket writes the representation the ledger already holds so it adds nothing to the split, and asserts the webhook still writes exactly one representation so the claim goes stale loudly. NO GIFT IS COUNTED TWICE (STOP condition 4): the invoice is the money record and the timeline entry REFERENCES it - `amount: null` (the field the webhook writes in DOLLARS and the field any future money reader would reach for) plus `invoiceId`, with `invoiceAmountCents` as a display mirror named so nothing in this repository sums it, and a sweep asserts no surface reduces `contactActivities` as money. `contacts.totalDonated` is still bumped in dollars, unchanged, because it is the contact's own running total and the same field the webhook increments for a Stripe gift. A GIFT WITH NO EMAIL IS RECORDED AND SAID SO: refusing would lose the church's own record of a cash gift from someone who has no address - money it really received, which belongs on the dashboard and in the books - so the invoice is written with `recipientEmail: ''`, `visibleToMember: false` comes back to the caller, and the CRM dialog names the consequence BEFORE the save. An empty stored email can never match anybody: the history route refuses an empty caller outright, the statement generator skips an empty recipient, and both GDPR paths guard on a non-empty subject email. No npm dependency, no theme token and no new primitive was installed, and NO primitive was composed into AdminCRM - it is the eighth hand-rolled file and is carded separately. ONE FILE THIS TICKET EDITS IS DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED IN `entries`, exactly as THE-349 left the same kind of edit unrecorded: THE-342's read-honesty guard suite, whose path carries a ticket number that is itself a record in this directory, and the no-index guard forbids naming one record from another in a structural field - so recording it would be an index by another name. What the edit is: that suite's `adminCrmDigest` becomes `adminCrmDigests`, an ACCEPTED SET holding THE-342's value AND THE-350's, and the test that read it becomes a set membership check whose failure message names every accepted value and the ticket that recorded it. APPENDED, NEVER SUBSTITUTED - the #422/#434 rule this repo already paid for: CI runs against `refs/pull/N/merge`, so a file another ticket legitimately lands on holds a different value on the merge ref than on this branch, and `main` went red for everyone the last time a digest was replaced instead of added. A digest that is NEITHER - a ticket editing the CRM without recording why - still fails, which is the entire threat the pin was built for. Nothing else in that suite moved: the two assertions carrying #482's work are untouched and now measure the file on disk rather than trusting a hash to stand in for them, and its emoji sweep is what kept the house markers out of this ticket's edit to `useCRMQueries.ts`.

entries.why: THE-350 OWNS this file and this is the state it leaves it in. THE-342 recorded the previous digest to say "this ticket did not open the CRM component"; THE-350 does open it, because the founder's manual-donation bug is IN it. Four changes, all inside `addActivity` and the Add Activity dialog. (1) THE LEDGER WRITE HAPPENS FIRST AND DECIDES: `authFetch('/api/donations/manual')` runs before any CRM write, and a refusal throws, so a failed gift writes NOTHING - no timeline entry, no `totalDonated` bump, no `lastDonationAt`. The opposite ordering is the founder's bug wearing a different shape. Asserted by ORDER, as three indices inside the located function body, not by presence. (2) THE ACTIVITY LINKS RATHER THAN DUPLICATES: `amount: null`, plus `invoiceId` and `invoiceAmountCents`, the latter a display mirror in CENTS under a name no money reader in this repository touches - the CRM cannot read `invoices` (admin-read-only, gated on `manageAccounting`) so the timeline needs the figure locally to draw the row, and it is rendered through `formatCents` and never through the file's own dollar `fmt()`. Rows written before this ticket, and every Stripe gift the webhook logs, still carry dollars in `amount` and still render through `fmt` - the branch is two-armed, not a replacement. (3) A FAILED WRITE SURFACES AND KEEPS THE INPUT: a new `activityError` state renders a `role="alert"` banner inside the dialog; the dialog stays open, the typed amount and description stay in their fields, and the catch block sets neither `setShowAddActivity(false)` nor `setActForm(...)` - both live in the success path only. `notifyError` is still called so the failure reaches the console/toast path every other write here uses. THE-321's `saveState` machine is the model and `sendEmail` twenty lines below is the precedent this mirrors. (4) TWO NOTICES IN THE DIALOG: what a recorded gift now reaches, and - when the contact has no email address - that the giver will never see it in their own donation history and no receipt can reach them, with the remedy (add an email first) named. Both are TEXT, not controls: this ticket adds no tappable target at all, which is asserted rather than assumed. Every colour is a semantic token (`bg-danger-tint`, `text-danger`, `text-danger-strong`, `border-danger`, `text-gold`, `bg-surface-tint`, `text-body`, `text-strong`); the seven hexes already in the file are pinned BY VALUE so an eighth cannot appear and none of them can move. NO PRIMITIVE WAS COMPOSED IN, deliberately: `ui/alert` is the right primitive for both notices and is what a follow-up should use, but this file is the eighth hand-rolled file and is carded separately, and a single `<Alert>` beside eight hand-rolled panels in the same PR as a money-ledger write is a visual pass smuggled in behind a data fix. The only `ui/` import in the file is still the `Collapsible` #482 introduced, asserted as an exact list. #482's work is untouched and re-measured rather than trusted to a hash: the payment-links disclaimer still collapses with its trigger sentence and THE-249's panel body byte-for-byte, `keepMounted` is still there, and the Contacts/Roles switcher is still ONE `subTabBar` definition rendered on both sub-views.

THE-350 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file. `ContactActivity` gains two optional fields - `invoiceId` and `invoiceAmountCents` - and `amount`'s doc comment is corrected in place to say what it now means: DOLLARS for a Stripe gift the webhook logs and for every manual activity written BEFORE this ticket, and ALWAYS NULL on a gift recorded by hand since it, because the money record for such a gift is the invoice the row points at. The field docs are where the double-count rule has to live: `amount` is the name a future reader would reach for, and `invoiceAmountCents` says in its own name that it is a display mirror in cents rather than a second money-bearing figure. NO READ, NO QUERY AND NO FETCH SHAPE MOVED - THE-342's four `orderBy(documentId())` clauses, `CRM_FETCH_LIMIT`, the scoping branch, the super-admin gate, the `NO_TENANT_SCOPE_MESSAGE` throw and the merge are all byte-identical, and THE-342's own guards still measure them. NO EMOJI: THE-342 sweeps the RAW source of this file for the pictograph range, so the house markers this repo writes into docblocks everywhere else are deliberately absent here, and the two additions are written in plain emphasis instead.

THE-350 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-349 owned the one before it and THE-348 the one before that. `RULES_PINNERS_NOW` goes 66 -> 67 and this ticket's guard suite joins `RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE` beside THE-349's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-350 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere: it FOUND that the fix must not touch the rules - the invoices rule gates on `manageAccounting` while a CRM admin holds `manageCRM`, and loosening it would give every CRM admin write access to the money ledger in a file that auto-deploys with no emulator tests - so the write moved to the Admin SDK behind a route that checks the permission itself, and the rule is ASSERTED as it stands.
